lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: side ratios determined by similarity, not by size
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: side ratios determined by similarity, not by size

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: A 3-4-5 triangle, θ opposite the side 3. Find sin θ.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 26 and one leg 10. Find the other leg.
Express sin 62° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 28°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 62°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 152°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 118°, because the angles are supplementary

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: From a point 4 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 3 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
A right triangle has legs 16 and 30 and hypotenuse 34. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 16. Find sin θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
A right triangle has legs 32 and 60. Find the hypotenuse.
Express sin 75° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 75°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 105°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 165°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 15°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: From a point 45 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 24 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 40 and 42 and hypotenuse 58. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 40. Find tan θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
